item.title: The Hidden Simplicity of the Classical Limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.31369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the classical limit of two-to-two massive-scalar amplitudes at all orders of perturbation theory. We compute these amplitudes in the probe limit for several theories: a family of scalar theories, electrodynamics, and $\mathcal{N}=8$ supergravity with half-BPS matter. We show that related multiple-emission classical amplitudes obey a simple factorization derivable from the usual factorization of quantum amplitudes. The classical factorization, which reflects the second-order nature of classical dynamics, holds in more general theories --- including gravity. We further show that both the multiple-emission and the two-to-two classical amplitudes have a simple organization in terms of weighted trees. This allows a recursive computation to all orders in the probe limit. The probe's trajectory emerges as a generating function of trees. The required boundary conditions are given by the Feynman $i \varepsilon$ prescription, leading to a novel worldline Green's function. In our approach, the rich classical dynamics arises from simple combinatorics.
item.dc:creator: Yilber Fabian Bautista, Stefano De Angelis, David A. Kosower, Donal O'Connell, Matteo Sergola

item.title: Bootstrapping two-loop $\beta$-functions for bosonic and heterotic strings
item.description: arXiv:2611.31372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Beyond one loop, $\beta$-functions of non-linear $\sigma$-models are hard to compute directly. We obtain them instead as a gradient flow of the low-energy effective action, whose coupling-space metric is fixed exclusively by symmetry. This gives a two-parameter family of O$(d,d)$-covariant, two-loop $\beta$-functions that covers the bosonic and heterotic string at once. Because only symmetry enters, the method opens a route to higher loops. As an application, we derive the two-loop RG flow of the integrable $\eta$- and $\lambda$-deformations; for the heterotic string, the correction is half of the bosonic one.
item.dc:creator: Achilleas Gitsis, Falk Hassler

item.title: A Kerr-black-hole worldline action to $\mathcal{O}(G^5)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.31377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a worldline action which correctly reproduces Kerr-black-hole dynamics up to fifth order in Newton's constant in a physical post-Minkowskian counting. This encompasses operators up to second order in the Riemann curvature tensor and up to fourth order in the spin tensor. Doing so entails performing the full effective-field-theory computation of the amplitude for a gravitational-wave scattering off of a spinning compact object up to four-loop order, and matching the result to the predictions from linear black hole perturbation theory. Quadratic-in-curvature operators which must be added to match successfully include time-reversal anti-symmetric ones at linear and cubic spin orders, capturing absorption across the black hole horizon, and conservative quadratic-in-spin ones. As an immediate application of our action, we compute the leading-order change in spin magnitude, and reproduce the leading change in mass, for a Kerr black hole in a scattering event with a second compact body, considering a generic orientation of the black hole's spin.
item.dc:creator: Yilber Fabian Bautista, Mathias Driesse, Kays Haddad, Gustav Uhre Jakobsen

item.title: Circulating currents around orbifolded defects
item.description: arXiv:2611.31391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate holographic monodromy defects with five dimensional orbifold singularities which lift to smooth and supersymmetric ten dimensional geometries. Such geometries have been of recent interest in spindle compactifications and have been interpreted as generalized Gukov-Witten defects. They are constructed by taking an orbifold of previously considered holographic monodromy defects on a space with a conical excess angle, and are not adiabatically connected to the empty anti-de Sitter vacuum. The the orbifold action acts nontrivially both on the five dimensional base as well as the five-sphere. We calculate one-point functions and anomaly coefficients as a function of the monodromies and orbifold data. Surprisingly, we discover that defects exhibit nonzero circulating currents even when all monodromies are turned off, unlike defects adiabatically connected to the vacuum, and therefore correspond to 1/8-BPS excited states. Comparing defects with nontrivial bulk topology we find that the A-type anomaly coefficient is always larger than those with trivial topology, while the B-type coefficient can be either larger or smaller.
item.dc:creator: Matthew M. Roberts

item.title: The Schwarzschild-Kerr crossover of high overtone quasinormal modes
item.description: arXiv:2611.31394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A slowly rotating black hole is close to a nonrotating one, but its highly damped quasinormal spectrum is not. The Schwarzschild approximation holds only up to overtone numbers of order $\chi^{-4/3}$, where $\chi$ is the dimensionless spin. We find that the frequency shift at this scale is a universal function, derived from the wave boundary conditions with an error estimate. It is given by the spectrum of a sextic oscillator, via the correspondence between ordinary differential equations and integrable models. It recovers the Schwarzschild $\log 3$ and organizes the singular Kerr coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Yasuyuki Hatsuda

item.title: Refined R\'enyi Entropy from Replica-Geometry Tensor Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.31398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Holographic tensor networks are a central route to understanding the mechanism behind the holographic duality, but standard fixed-graph constructions with maximally entangled links face a structural obstacle. Their leading entanglement spectra are flat, so their R\'enyi entropies do not depend on the replica index. This is in sharp contrast with holographic conformal field theories, where a tensionful cosmic brane makes the refined R\'enyi entropy $n$-dependent. Capturing this replica dependence is therefore an important test of tensor-network descriptions of holographic entanglement. We construct an explicit family of replica-dependent geodesic graphs that reproduces this behavior while keeping the links maximally entangled. For each replica index $n$, geodesics are emitted from the replicated boundary with the same local, isotropic intersection measure. They perfectly tessellate the selected replica geometry, so the $n$-dependence of their intersection counts comes from the geometry. Tensor-network models on these graphs reproduce the cosmic-brane prescription for refined R\'enyi entropy by counting crossing threads. Their cross-copy endpoint density also agrees, in CFT$_2$, with a boundary reconstruction within the additive linear combination proposal, providing a check beyond the total entropy. In higher dimensions, we further obtain an analytic large-separation decay law for this density.
item.dc:creator: Qiang Wen, Haocheng Zhong, Yiwei Zhong

item.title: Elliptic spin Ruijsenaars--Schneider model via the Poisson reduction of the affine Heisenberg double
item.description: arXiv:2611.31405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct the Hamiltonian structure of the elliptic spin Ruijsenaars--Schneider model with dynamical inhomogeneities by Poisson reduction of the affine Heisenberg double extended by an affine oscillator manifold. This construction extends the Heisenberg double approach to spin Ruijsenaars--Schneider models from the hyperbolic to the elliptic case. We solve the moment map constraint and derive the Poisson algebras of the invariant Lax operator and spin variables. A realization with finitely many degrees of freedom is obtained by evaluating and localizing the invariant oscillators at distinct points of the affine parameter. Consistency requires these points to be dynamical so that their nontrivial Poisson brackets with the spin variables cancel derivative terms that would otherwise obstruct closure of the Poisson bracket on finitely many degrees of freedom. The resulting Poisson brackets and Hamiltonian coincide with those recently obtained from the elliptic Coulomb branch of the necklace quiver. Our construction thus provides an independent derivation of this Hamiltonian structure and establishes a direct link between Poisson reductions and Coulomb branches.
item.dc:creator: Gleb Arutyunov, Lukas Hardi, Davide Polvara

item.title: Flat Space Entanglement from Wedge Holography
item.description: arXiv:2611.31414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study holographic entanglement entropy in three-dimensional flat space by combining wedge holography with a controlled flat limit of AdS end-of-the-world branes. The limit takes a wedge of AdS$_4$ bounded by two AdS$_3$ branes to a Randall-Sundrum-like configuration of two flat branes, and the entanglement entropy of an interval in the two-dimensional corner CFT becomes that of an interval at null infinity of the branes. The result has the functional form of the entanglement entropy of a two-dimensional Carrollian CFT, the proposed holographic dual of gravity in asymptotically flat three-dimensional spacetimes. However, the inferred central charges yield $c_M=0$ and $c_L\to\infty$ in the flat limit. Adding a gravitational Chern-Simons term produces a $c_M$-like contribution, but we still find $c_L\to\infty$ and $c_M\to0$ in this limit. Moreover, the corresponding extremal surfaces do not approach the swing surfaces proposed by Song and collaborators. Instead, they collapse onto null rays along null infinity. We argue that both features are generic for flat limits of AdS/CFT. They follow from entanglement entropy being a property of the domain of dependence and from the equality of causal and entanglement wedges for intervals in the vacuum.
item.dc:creator: Robert C. Myers, Bruno Sivilotti

item.title: A spin chain as a deformed conformal field theory: an ODE/IM approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.31417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ODE/IM correspondence relates ordinary differential equations to integrable quantum field theories in the continuum. We ask whether it extends to integrable spin chains of finite length $N$. We analyse the twisted XXZ chain at a special anisotropy and twist, focusing on states in its Lee--Yang scaling sector. Their finite-size corrections are expected to come from the Lee--Yang conformal field theory deformed by irrelevant operators, and with the help of the ODE/IM correspondence we make this deformation explicit for the energy and the local conserved charges. Near each of the two edges of the distribution of the Bethe roots, the chain behaves as one chirality of the Lee--Yang theory in a generalised Gibbs ensemble, whose chemical potentials depend on $N$. The ODE/IM correspondence describes each of these ensembles by a cubic oscillator, whose coefficients we determine as series in $1/N$. The two chiralities are not independent: finite-size effects couple them, so that the charges of each shift the chemical potentials of the other. This turns out to be a generalised $T\bar T$-type interaction. Solving this coupling self-consistently, we obtain the energy and the local conserved charges of the chain as series in $1/N$, with no free parameters. We verify these series against the Bethe ansatz, for the ground state and for an excited state.
item.dc:creator: Sujay K. Ashok, Nicol\`o Primi, Roberto Tateo

item.title: Topological Phase Transition of $ F_{\alpha }{}^{\gamma } F^{\alpha \beta } F_{\beta }{}^{\eta } \ F^{\lambda \mu } R_{\gamma \eta \lambda \mu } $ AdS Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.31433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic criticality and topological properties of four-dimensional charged anti-de Sitter black holes in the presence of a nonminimal electromagnetic-curvature interaction of the form \(F_{\alpha}{}^{\gamma}F^{\alpha\beta}F_{\beta}{}^{\eta}F^{\lambda\mu}R_{\gamma\eta\lambda\mu}\). Treating the coupling perturbatively to first order, we construct the corrected black hole solutions and derive their thermodynamic quantities in the extended phase space. Conventional critical behavior is examined through the criticality conditions for the Hawking temperature in both canonical and grand canonical ensembles. We then use thermodynamic topology to investigate the global structure of equilibrium configurations and its dependence on the thermodynamic parameters. In the canonical ensemble, two distinct regimes emerge: a noncritical region characterized by a total winding number \(W=+1\), and a critical region with \(W=0\). In the grand canonical ensemble, three distinct regimes are identified according to the electric potential. Interestingly, the low- and intermediate-potential regions share the same topological number, \(W=+1\), although conventional critical points occur only in the intermediate-potential region. The high-potential region, by contrast, is characterized by \(W=0\) and exhibits no conventional critical behavior. Our findings show that thermodynamic topology provides a global characterization of equilibrium configurations that complements conventional temperature-based criticality analysis, and that the global winding number alone does not uniquely determine the existence of conventional critical points.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Sadeghi, Faramarz Rahmani

item.title: The Relaxation of Quantum Near-Extremal Black Holes. (I) Microcanonical States, Pruning of Quasinormal Modes, and the Aretakis Instability
item.description: arXiv:2611.31459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The late-time relaxation of a near-extremal black hole is classically governed by an infinite tower of purely damped quasinormal modes. This poses a puzzle: the higher overtones decay at rates much larger than the energy $E$ of the black hole above extremality, so they would need black hole states below the extremal mass. We resolve it by including the quantum fluctuations that become large when $E$ falls below a scale $E_b$. We compute the retarded Green's function of a probe of conformal dimension $\Delta$ in a black hole of fixed energy, and find that each classical mode splits into a pair of poles with real parts set by $E_b$. The perturbed black hole decays as an unstable quantum system, and a pair is a resonance, i.e., a quasinormal mode, only if its energy lies within the accessible black hole spectrum. This prunes the tower to finitely many modes, all damped faster than $\Delta^2E_b$, and below $E=\Delta^2E_b/2$ none is left. For generic $\Delta$, the response of the black hole decays first as $t^{-2\Delta}$ and finally as $t^{-3/2}$, with an exponential stage in between if $E\gg\Delta^2E_b$. The same quantum effects bear on the Aretakis instability of extremal black holes, in which transverse derivatives of a perturbation grow without bound on the horizon. Like the tower of modes, it originates in the scale invariance of the classical throat, which the quantum fluctuations break. The $t^{-2\Delta}$ decay, which is the boundary counterpart of the Aretakis growth, ends by $t\sim1/E_b$, when the throat ceases to be classical, and by then horizon derivatives have grown only to a finite value. Their unbounded growth is an artifact of taking the semiclassical limit before the late-time one, two limits that in quantum mechanics do not commute.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Emparan, Sameer Murthy, Stefano Trezzi

item.title: Exact Scalar and Fermionic Propagators in a Uniform Electric Background
item.description: arXiv:2611.31528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By implementing an analytical hybrid framework that combines the Ritus eigenfunction technique with Schwinger's proper-time formalism, we construct exact propagators for charged scalar and fermionic fields in a constant, homogeneous, external electric field in four-dimensional Euclidean space. A central advantage of this approach is that the resulting propagators retain a four-dimensional momentum representation after the spectral summation, connecting the structure of the Ritus basis with the operator formulation of the proper-time method, without requiring the full traditional derivation of Schwinger's approach and the coordinate restrictions originally associated with the Ritus method for fermions. The translationally non-invariant component emerging after the Laguerre-polynomial summation is isolated through a suitable change of variables, yielding translationally invariant kernels and maintaining the background field strength unchanged. As a consistency check, we successfully rederive Schwinger's seminal expression for the fermionic pair production rate.
item.dc:creator: Emerson B. S. Corr\^ea

item.title: Radiation from periods: Bremsstrahlung functions, wound loops, latitudes and integral constraints in ABJM
item.description: arXiv:2611.31555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Bremsstrahlung functions of the 1/2BPS and 1/6BPS Wilson lines of ABJM theory measure their response to small deformations. We show that a single geometric object, the spectral curve of the localisation matrix model, captures both of them in closed form, together with the planar wound and latitude Wilson loops at any complex winding and framing. The fermionic function turns out to be a period of the second kind: a single hypergeometric function, which solves a second-order differential equation and is quasimodular. The bosonic one is not a period but a ratio of periods. At every coupling it is the smaller of the two, so radiation grows along the defect flow from the bosonic to the fermionic line. The key role is played by a new observable, the winding velocity, which turns out to be the 't Hooft coupling shifted by four times the fermionic function. It is at the same time the winding derivative of the wound loop and the curvature of the latitude, and the curve captures it in both incarnations through its logarithmic periods and through its periods with two charges. It is also a datum of the defect conformal field theory on the 1/2BPS line, since it fixes a new integrated four-point function of the tilt operators. All results extend to ABJ theory when the ranks of the gauge groups are not equal.
item.dc:creator: Michelangelo Preti

item.title: New relations of tree-level string amplitudes from the massless prescription
item.description: arXiv:2611.31580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discover new relations between the string corrections to $(m+1)$-point field-theory amplitudes and $m$-point string amplitudes at tree level from the massless prescription of vertex operators.
item.dc:creator: Chen Huang, Yi-Xiao Tao

item.title: All the Positive Energy Correlators
item.description: arXiv:2611.31587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a framework to systematically obtain the full set of positivity bounds on multi-point energy correlators for sources of arbitrary spin. The constraints are organized in a family of positive operators $\mathscr{E}^{(N,k)}$, with $k=0,\ldots,\lfloor N/2\rfloor$. Our approach provides outer bounds, which exclude correlators that violate the positivity of $\mathscr{E}^{(N,k)}$, and inner bounds, obtained by constructing ensembles of consistent collider events via linear programming. Both methods converge to each other as numerical precision increases. This approach, in particular, characterizes the allowed higher-point correlators once lower-point correlators are determined. We illustrate this through several examples, including bounds on multipoles of the three-point energy correlator in QCD derived from measurements of one- and two-point correlators at LEP.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Ricci, Marc Riembau, Minho Son

item.title: The Eigenfunction Method to Calculate the Klein--Gordon Propa-gator in an Inhomogeneous Magnetic Field
item.description: arXiv:2611.31630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we use the Eigenfunction method (Ritus' method) to calculate the Klein--Gordon propagator under an external magnetic field with an exponential damping factor $b$, in a four-dimensional Euclidean space. We write the propagator of scalar field in terms of plane waves and Laguerre polynomials. Also the eigenvalues associated to differential operator show the quantization in the $\mathrm{xy}$-plane through the Landau levels. We apply the calculated propagator to the mass parameter of an interacting boson system under an exponentially decaying magnetic field.
item.dc:creator: Emerson B. S. Corr\^{e}, Mateus G. Lima, Suellen. C. Q. Arruda

item.title: The Matrix in Pieces: Complete BFSS Scattering at Finite Rank
item.description: arXiv:2611.31649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As two matrix blocks separate in Banks-Fischler-Shenker-Susskind matrix quantum mechanics, the modes connecting them develop a growing excitation gap. Supersymmetry cancels their leading vacuum energy, so blocks in internal bound states can scatter as composite particles. We prove that these particle channels are asymptotically complete for the physical relative Hamiltonian at each fixed finite rank $N\ge 2$. Because a block can itself break up as its center moves away from the others, the proof must control motion on both scales. Inverse powers of the matrix radius control derivatives along internal flat directions, while the growing gap suppresses excitations between blocks. Propagation estimates then allow us to resolve successive breakups by induction on the block rank. The incoming and outgoing wave operators each have range equal to the absolutely continuous subspace, and the singular-continuous subspace vanishes. The scattering operator is thus unitary when each constituent can occupy any of its internal bound states. For a normalized incoming state of zero-energy constituents, the outgoing probability missing from the zero-energy channels equals the inclusive probability of producing at least one constituent with positive internal energy.
item.dc:creator: Mai Qi

item.title: Second-order localization and intersecting O6-planes in scale-separated AdS vacua
item.description: arXiv:2611.31660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct explicit periodic second-order localization corrections to scale-separated AdS$_4$ vacua of massive type IIA supergravity on $T^6/(\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2)$. At first order, the corrections from different O6-plane families simply add. The interactions between intersecting families first enter at second order and could obstruct the continuation of the solution. We find explicit solutions for the warp factor, dilaton, full internal metric and required form fields, including the terms generated by these interactions. The metric at second order contains off-diagonal components. With a common regularization of the singular source terms, we verify the full field equations and the conditions required for a solution on a compact space. Using the pure-spinor formalism, we find that the second-order fields satisfy the supersymmetry conditions accessible at the retained orders.
item.dc:creator: Aravind Aikot, Timm Wrase

item.title: $AdS$ Leading Regge Trajectory from String Field Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.31678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the $AdS$ mass of the leading Regge trajectory in superstring backgrounds $AdS_5\times S^5$, $AdS_4\times\mathbb{CP}^3$, and $AdS_3\times S^3\times{\cal M}_4$ with pure Ramond-Ramond (RR) flux for both ${\cal M}_4=S^3\times S^1$ and ${\cal M}_4=T^4$, to the second order in the expansion with respect to the background RR flux by solving the linearized equations of motion in closed superstring field theory. The $AdS_5$ and $AdS_4$ results are in a complete agreement with those obtained from the integrability approach to dual gauge theories, thereby providing a nontrivial check of the holographic duality beyond supersymmetry-protected quantities.
item.dc:creator: Minjae Cho, Jo\~{a}o Gomide, Jaroslav Scheinpflug, Xi Yin

item.title: BPS baryonic tubes in chiral perturbation theory minimally coupled with electrodynamics and a novel crossover
item.description: arXiv:2611.31719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a novel first-order BPS system (whose solutions are automatically solutions of the second-order field equations) in chiral perturbation theory (CPT) in $(3+1)$ dimensions. These BPS configurations describe baryonic tubes carrying a chiral current along the tubes themselves. Such baryonic tubes can be either homogeneous or modulated along the $z$-axis. We analyze the leading term in CPT, which is the $SU(2)$ non-linear sigma model minimally coupled to electrodynamics. These exact solutions are qualitatively different from the available analytic description of baryonic tubes since, due to their BPS nature, the positions of the energy-density peaks can be arbitrary. In contrast (in the case of the known solutions in the literature), the energy-density peaks' positions are fixed. We compare these two types of baryonic configurations; the relevant parameter that determines which one is energetically favored is the baryonic charge density: for low densities, the old solutions are favorable, while for high densities these novel BPS tubes are energetically favored. The inclusion of the electromagnetic field (together with the corresponding back-reaction on the baryonic tubes) can also be treated analytically. We discuss the differences in the electromagnetic field distribution between the two regions (low and high baryonic density). The analysis of potential terms for the chiral field is detailed in Appendix B.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Canfora, Mart\'in Garrido, Pablo Pais

item.title: Hadron structure in $1+1$ dimensions from the infinite Hamiltonian lattice
item.description: arXiv:2611.31750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The internal structure of a hadron is encoded in matrix elements of operators between hadron states of definite momentum. In this paper, we develop a framework for computing such matrix elements in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories by working on an infinite spatial lattice. We apply the method to the massive Schwinger model. We benchmark our method against discretized lightcone quantization (DLCQ) at $\theta = 0$, and then use the lattice to study hadrons at $\theta\neq 0$, where DLCQ does not apply. We compute parton distribution functions and gravitational form factors, and both show signatures of hadrons becoming large, loosely-bound states when we set $m$ greater than the critical mass $m_c$ and approach $\theta = \pi$ from below. Moreover, we see the gravitational form factor change from that of a free boson to that of a free Majorana fermion when we set $\theta = \pi$ and approach the 2D Ising critical point at $m=m_c$ from below.
item.dc:creator: Ross Dempsey

item.title: A cubic theory of gravity with quasitopological-like properties for compactified cosmologies
item.description: arXiv:2611.31758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify a cubic combination of curvature invariants in dimension $D=7$ that when added to the Einstein-Hilbert action, yields a healthy cosmological evolution in four dimensions after compactification on a constant-curvature internal space of dimension three. For generic backgrounds it leads to fourth-order field equations, nevertheless, on a warped product of a spatially flat, homogeneous and isotropic four-dimensional universe with a constant-curvature space of radius $b(t)$, the constraint is of first order in the scale factor $a(t)$ and in $b(t)$, while the remaining equations are of second order. Requiring this property uniquely singles out the cubic theory. We study the solutions describing a four-dimensional de Sitter Universe in direct product with an internal space of stabilized radius and evaluate its linear stability under time-dependent perturbations, showing that for a given sign of the curvature of the internal space, stability of the static solution fixes the sign of the higher curvature coupling. We also argue that linearized scalar perturbations depending on the spatial coordinates obey equations with at most two time derivatives. Finally, we numerically evolve the homogeneous and isotropic system non-linearly and present evidence that for a positive bare cosmological term $\Lambda_0$ and a hyperbolic compact space, the singularity formation present in GR in this ansatz is pushed into the future by increasing the higher-curvature coupling.
item.dc:creator: Vicente Aguilar, Fabrizio Canfora, Vicente Garc\'ia, Alex Giacomini, Julio Oliva

item.title: Beyond the Thermodynamic-Volume Limit in Holographic Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.31761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the large black hole regime, holographic complexity obeys a thermodynamic-volume scaling law, while the finite-size approach to this limit remains unresolved. In this Letter, we develop an analytic description of finite-size corrections to this scaling for complexity of formation in the complexity=volume (CV) proposal of odd-dimensional equal-spinning Myers-Perry-AdS black holes. We find that the leading finite-size correction retains state dependence that is absent from the limiting thermodynamic-volume law. This correction changes sign at a distinguished Critical Horizon Ratio (CHR), where the generic leading finite-size contribution vanishes and convergence to the thermodynamic-volume law is correspondingly accelerated. We further determine the dimension dependence of the CHR analytically, showing that it approaches a finite nonextremal value at large dimension with a calculable leading finite-dimensional correction. These results show that the finite-size approach can provide a new probe of holographic structure, motivating its exploration across different realizations of holographic complexity and its eventual characterization in the dual field theory.
item.dc:creator: Di Wu, Robert B. Mann

item.title: NS5-branes and the black hole/string transition
item.description: arXiv:2611.31945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near to the onset of BTZ black hole formation in string theory is a large ensemble of 6d BPS supergravity solutions sourced by slightly separated fundamental strings and Neveu-Schwarz fivebranes. We extend the construction of these geometries to include gauge excitations of the fivebranes, and then study the energetics of D-string solitons in relation to the deconfinement transition of little strings, which are the natural non-abelian degrees of freedom that deconfine in the transition to the black hole phase.
item.dc:creator: Asad Fayiz, Emil J. Martinec

item.title: M5-branes wrapped on topological disks from maximal 7D gauged supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.31947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study new supersymmetric $AdS_5 \times \Sigma$ solutions for $\Sigma$ being a topological disk from the maximal gauged supergravity in seven dimensions with $CSO(p,q,5-p-q)$ gauge groups. These gauged supergravities can be obtained from consistent truncations of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $H^{p,q} \circ T^{5-p-q}$. We find a number of solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ and $SO(3,2)$ gauge groups as well as $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetric solutions from $SO(5)$ and $SO(4,1)$ gauge groups. Solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetry preserve $16$ supercharges while the other solutions preserve only $8$ supercharges. Although some of the solutions give a holographic description of the dual $N=1$ SCFTs in four dimensions with finite central charges, most of the solutions describe codimension-2 defects within $N=(2,0)$ theories in six dimensions. For solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ gauge group for which a complete truncation ansatz of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $S^4$ is known, we also uplift the solutions to eleven dimensions and compute the holographic central charge of the dual four-dimensional $N=1$ SCFT with $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Patharadanai Nuchino, Parinya Karndumri

item.title: Entanglement structure in conformal Y-junctions
item.description: arXiv:2611.32062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how entanglement constrains energy transmission in conformal Y-junctions using holographic and free-field models. We define pairwise effective central charges from mutual information as a natural extension of the interface entanglement coefficient. For holographic junctions, we formulate a branched RT prescription and show that the resulting entropies satisfy monogamy of mutual information. We find that the pairwise effective central charge does not always bound the corresponding energy transmission, but a correction involving finite tripartite information restores the bound, with a sharp coefficient determined by limiting saturation. Free-boson and Dirac-fermion junctions also violate the pairwise bound, but the tripartite correction fails because the tripartite information is positive or vanishing, respectively. Analytic limits and numerical results instead support a candidate square-root correction based on L-entropy, which vanishes in the holographic complete-leg prescription considered here. We discuss the possibility of a common multipartite information bound in general conformal junctions.
item.dc:creator: Yan Liu, You-Jie Zeng

item.title: Resolvent reconstruction of minimal strings beyond KdV II: D series models
item.description: arXiv:2611.32150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Three-state Potts gravity and tetracritical Ising gravity have the same central charge and the same conformal spectral curve. What distinguishes their amplitudes once a handle or a boundary is added? We answer this question by extending Johnson's differential-equation approach, in the reconstruction form developed in Part I for the reduced KP hierarchies, to D-series minimal strings. Their spatial operator is a pseudo-differential pencil with a nonlocal Pfaffian term, and the classical energy acquires a second pole at zero momentum. Regularity at both poles fixes the quantum corrections uniquely, ordinary string equations supply them, and the ordinary D flows add boundaries in a way that matches the tau function. At genus one the closed free energy follows from the pencil as a sum of logarithms of critical-value velocities. The two theories differ through the origin of the curve, which the D theory counts as two canonical directions, and through the pairing of every point with its reflection. We follow the origin contribution through the free energies to genus three, the one-holed torus and the torus one-point amplitudes, and in the primary range the latter reproduce the formulas conjectured from worldsheet numerics for both series.
item.dc:creator: Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar

item.title: Holographic Entanglement Entropy of Network CFT
item.description: arXiv:2611.32224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Miao et al. \cite{Guo:2025sbm, Guo:2026prm} proposed the AdS/NCFT correspondence, which explores the gravity dual of conformal field theories defined on networks. While previous studies investigated this model within Einstein and Gauss-Bonnet gravity (first- and second-order Lovelock gravity), in this paper, we generalize the framework to higher-order Lovelock gravity and more complex network structures. We derive the extremal and junction conditions for generalized Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) surfaces in third-order Lovelock gravity, which can be naturally extended to arbitrary higher-order Lovelock theories. Focusing on a network model comprising one node and three branches, we numerically investigate the relationship between the network holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and gravitational coupling coefficients. Furthermore, by analyzing the HEE across various network configurations, we find that the primary structural feature affecting the network HEE is the presence of internal nodes within line-shaped networks. Our results indicate that the network HEE decreases as the number or depth of internal branches increases.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Rong Deng, Jie Yang

item.title: D0-brane bound states in Matrix theory: nonperturbative bounds on matrix extent, noncommutativity and spatial shape
item.description: arXiv:2611.32333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Matrix theory, a single eleven-dimensional supergraviton is associated with a BPS bound state of D0-branes. Assuming the existence of a normalized physical BPS state, we derive nonperturbative bounds on its matrix extent, noncommutativity and spatial shape from supersymmetry in the BFSS model. The probability of matrix configurations smaller than a fixed fraction of an explicit extent scale is exponentially suppressed in the square of the number $N$ of D0-branes. In Yang-Mills variables, this scale for the trace-normalized extent is of order the cube root of the 't Hooft coupling. Relative noncommutativity, measured by a dimensionless commutator ratio, has an expectation bounded by a quantity of order the inverse of $N$, and its probability of exceeding a sufficiently large fixed multiple of the inverse of $N$ vanishes at large $N$. Concentration of the matrix extent along a fixed number of principal directions fewer than nine at large $N$ requires the total extent relative to a corresponding reference scale to diverge in probability. It also requires relative noncommutativity to be suppressed more strongly than the inverse of $N$, in every fixed finite moment of order at least one. These bounds apply to the full quantum wave function, including off-diagonal matrix degrees of freedom, and constrain the quantum structure of D0-brane bound states and the possible large-$N$ matrix geometries in Matrix theory.
item.dc:creator: Tetsuyuki Muramatsu

item.title: The DBI critical electric field in stationary non-diagonal geometries
item.description: arXiv:2611.32378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the critical electric field for the holographic Schwinger effect in general stationary non-diagonal geometries. We show that, in such backgrounds, the DBI reality condition must be formulated in terms of the electric field measured in a local orthonormal frame, since the coordinate components of the field strength need not represent a purely electric field in that frame. The critical field measured in the orthonormal frame takes the universal value \(E_{\mathrm{proper},c}=T_F\), while its coordinate expression depends on the background geometry. The resulting critical field is independently confirmed by the holographic potential analysis, through the disappearance of the potential barrier. We further illustrate the general prescription using the planar limit and the global rotating Myers--Perry--AdS geometry, which exhibit different types of metric mixing.
item.dc:creator: Leila Shahkarami

item.title: Holographic Spread Complexity of a Probe Particle with General Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.32427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the holographic spread complexity of a massive particle probing global AdS$_3$ with general initial data. By constructing an adapted Hamiltonian, we map each bulk geodesic to a boundary Krylov dynamical pair, whose dynamics are governed solely by the conserved chiral charges. We find that, for generic initial data, the original identification $\dot{C}\sim p_\rho$ fails; instead, both the complexity and its growth rate depend nonlinearly on the bulk Noether charges. We systematically analyze this nonlinear encoding via several perturbative expansions. We further investigate two refined variants: the symmetry-resolved spread complexity, which restores the bulk radial $\pi$-periodicity, and the chiral spread complexity, which admits an exact closed form approaching the standard complexity at small angular momentum. Finally, by directly quantizing an effective AdS$_2$ theory, we obtain a new holographic interpretation of spread complexity in terms of the lapse function.
item.dc:creator: Zekun Qian, Zhehan Li, Jia Tian

item.title: Romans Mass from a $\mathrm{GL}(1,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2611.32437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an eleven-dimensional topological field theory with boundary whose edge modes are the dilaton and form fields of type IIA supergravity, including the Romans mass. The bulk action is the Chern--Simons functional of the superalgebra of the doubled formalism, completed by two brackets that are invisible in ten dimensions; it is unique up to normalization, contains no potentials, and the metric enters only through a boundary term. The Romans mass is the boundary value of a zero-form, like the other field strengths: it is varied, and its equation of motion is an eleven-form Gauss law with no ten-dimensional counterpart. The boundary term breaks the $GL(1,\mathbb{R})$ gauge symmetry to $O(1)$: the dilaton is the edge mode on $GL(1,\mathbb{R})/O(1)$, and $(-1)^{F_L}$, which reverses the Romans mass, becomes a gauge symmetry. The holonomies of the flat connection are monodromies of the dilaton and of $(-1)^{F_L}$, fixed classically by the D8-brane charges when the mass is nonzero, and the hypersurface dual to the $O(1)$ holonomy can end on reflection seven-branes. Since no field is self-dual, the reduction gives Romans' action off shell, while other boundary conditions of the same bulk give massless type IIA and dual formulations.
item.dc:creator: Euihun Joung, J. A. Rosabal

item.title: Entanglement island and Page curve for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.32438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the information paradox for one-sided asymptotically flat rotating Kerr black holes formed through gravitational collapse using the island prescription. Near the horizon, the dynamics of a scalar field can be described by an effective two-dimensional theory, which provides the framework for our analysis. We study how rotation affects the location of the island boundary $\partial I$, the Page time, and the scrambling time, treating non-extremal and extremal Kerr black holes separately. For non-extremal black holes, the emergence of an island prevents the unbounded growth of Hawking radiation entropy at late times and restores the unitary Page curve. We further find that the island boundary depends on the location of the cutoff surface, in contrast to the behaviour found for eternal Kerr black holes. In the extremal case, the late-time entanglement entropy of Hawking radiation approaches the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of the extremal black hole. Our results demonstrate the important role of black hole geometry in determining the behaviour of entanglement entropy and suggest that the island prescription provides a semiclassical resolution of the information paradox for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes.
item.dc:creator: Soumen Pari

item.title: Differential Equations for Feynman Integrals from Higher Residue Pairings
item.description: arXiv:2611.32544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a method for constructing differential equations for Feynman integrals directly from multivariate intersection numbers, without fibration. The large-$\varepsilon$ expansion of the intersection pairing, with $\varepsilon$ the dimensional regulator, is given by Saito's higher residue pairings, which localise at the critical points of a potential and admit closed multivariate formulae. In the Lee-Pomeransky representation, applying these formulae to Feynman integrals requires analytic regulators $\delta$ on the coordinate hyperplanes, and the physical limit $\delta \to 0$ is not manifest. Assuming that the regulated critical points are analytic in $\delta$, we show that, as $\delta \to 0$, they organise into sectors labelled by sets of pinched propagators. We derive closed formulae for the leading and first subleading higher residue pairings in this limit, written entirely in terms of unregulated sector data. These suffice to reconstruct differential systems at most linear in $\varepsilon$, including canonical ones, bypassing integration-by-parts identities. We apply the method to the massless planar four-point ladder families up to four loops and obtain their canonical differential equations, which are new at four loops.
item.dc:creator: Giacomo Brunello, Vsevolod Chestnov, Ben Page

item.title: Inflation at strong mixing as a connection problem: effective field theory, Stokes phenomenon and the cosmological collider
item.description: arXiv:2611.32612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a massive field strongly mixed with the curvature perturbation during inflation, in the regime where the latter is described at low energies by a single-field effective field theory (EFT) with a quadratic dispersion relation. What this EFT captures, and what lies beyond it, are encoded in a connection problem, which relates the solutions that define the vacuum at early times to those that describe observables at late times. We solve it with a general method that does not rely on an exact solution. An expansion in the inverse mixing, keeping both fields, yields the EFT as its leading order, with corrections under systematic control. It selects the vacuum of the EFT, fixes a phase that the EFT cannot determine on its own, and describes the heavy mode at all times. Particle production lies beyond all orders of this asymptotic expansion. We show that it arises from a Stokes phenomenon at the complex branch points of the dispersion relation and that, in a rotating basis of the two fields, it reduces to the familiar production of particles with half the heavy mass. A reflection symmetry of the equations of motion, combined with the canonical commutation relations, then determines all exponentially small effects exactly, and with them the solution of the connection problem, which combines particle production with a conversion between light and heavy quanta. Together with the expansion, these exact results give a compact analytical formula for the cosmological collider signal, whose exponential suppression, half of the usual Boltzmann one, directly reflects the halved mass of the produced particles. The expansion only requires a separation of scales and the adiabaticity of the heavy mode, while the reflection symmetry holds for many systems in de Sitter space. We therefore expect this approach to bring physical understanding and simple formulas well beyond the present case.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Garcia-Saenz, Yizhou Lu, S\'ebastien Renaux-Petel

item.title: Holographic Mutual Information in an Anisotropic Field Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.32637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate holographic mutual information in an anisotropic strongly coupled plasma within the framework of gauge/gravity duality. Considering both parallel and perpendicular strip configurations, we analyze the effects of temperature, anisotropy, strip lengths, and separation distance on the correlation structure between subsystems. For strips with equal lengths, we show that increasing temperature suppresses mutual information and reduces the size of the correlated region in the phase diagram. We find that the parallel configuration exhibits a monotonic behavior. However, the perpendicular configuration displays a more complex behavior resulting from the competition between the effects of energy density and pressure. Similar qualitative features are observed for strips with unequal lengths. Our results suggest that the directional dependence of the energy density and pressure plays an important role in the behavior of mutual information and may explain the nontrivial directional effects observed in the phase structure.
item.dc:creator: Mehri Rahimi, Masoumeh Tavakoli, Behrouz Mirza

item.title: The Wilson-loop formulation of Yang-Mills at finite mode truncation: a Level-Two structural bypass of the Gribov ambiguity
item.description: arXiv:2611.32690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The unfixed real-time Henstock-Kurzweil functional integral for truncated Yang-Mills removes the choice of a gauge surface, but gauge orbits remain objects of the formulation: that is a Level-One bypass of the Gribov ambiguity. This paper carries out a Level-Two bypass at finite mode truncation: the Wilson loops W(C) are taken as the fundamental variables, so that the configuration space is a space of loop data and no gauge field, gauge orbit, gauge-fixing condition or Faddeev-Popov determinant occurs anywhere in the formulation. Nine statements are proved and machine checked in Lean 4 without sorry, without admit and without new axioms: the loop algebra is commutative, conjugation-closed and gauge invariant, with bounded generators and the SU(2) Mandelstam identity; the truncated Yang-Mills action is an affine polynomial in the plaquette Wilson variables; loop-expressible observables are cylindrical; the oscillatory integrand is Henstock-Kurzweil integrable on every bounded loop-space box for every calibration, with the Lebesgue value; the integral is independent of gauge-fixing data and gauge copies are the same point of the loop formulation; for loop observables the Level-Two integral with respect to the push-forward measure coincides with the Level-One unfixed integral; the one-plaquette SU(2) check is proved in full, including the closed form 2J_1(beta)/beta; the SU(N) Mandelstam relations are derived in covariant trace form; and the finite-M integrals are projectively compatible, their limit existing as a linear functional, not a measure. No continuum limit, mass gap, confinement or Makeenko-Migdal equation is claimed; the Giles reconstruction theorem is cited only. The honest report records exactly where each proof stops.
item.dc:creator: Yu. N. Berdinsky

item.title: Baker-Akhiezer functions for Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system
item.description: arXiv:2611.32744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system is a counterpart of the trigonometric Ruijsenaars integrable system (associated with the root system $A_n$) for the root system $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$. It depends on the standard Macdonald parameters $q$ and $t$ as well as the Koornwinder (Askey-Wilson) parameters $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$. Different specializations of the parameters connect it to the other classical root systems from the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family. The eigenfunctions of the Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system are the symmetric Koornwinder polynomials; for certain values of the parameters $t$, $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ they coincide with the sum over the Weyl group of the Baker-Akhiezer functions introduced by O.A.\,Chalykh for the classical root system $BC_n$. The main idea behind this paper is to elucidate Chalykh's formalism and apply it to other affine root systems. We define Baker-Akhiezer functions for all root systems in the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family. We also present some explicit expressions for Baker-Akhiezer functions.
item.dc:creator: Liudmila Bishler

item.title: Cosmological Constant Screening from Quantum Horizon Chaos
item.description: arXiv:2611.32839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a microscopic mechanism for screening the cosmological constant through quantum chaos of the horizon degrees of freedom. We show that in a recently proposed quantum-horizon matrix model arXiv:2406.01466, the Schwarzschild--de Sitter junction completion arXiv:2608.21178 supports a gravitationally dressed soft mode that approaches the massless minimally coupled scalar of de Sitter gravity. Interactions among the microscopic horizon degrees of freedom provide a mechanism for force relaxation. Assuming a finite-memory force spectrum with nonzero regular low-frequency weight, the gravitationally dressed soft mode undergoes Brownian diffusion after momentum relaxation. The resulting bosonic coarse-grained entropy supplements the background entropy arising from fermionic parton microstates. We propose that their sum defines the total thermodynamic entropy, which can be identified with the Gibbons--Hawking entropy of the backreacted causal horizon. Entropy generation during the diffusion regime then leads to infrared screening of the effective cosmological constant, with a universal entropy--variance coefficient agreeing with that of Kitazawa and collaborators. Radiative lifting of the soft mode provides a possible mechanism for terminating the screening regime.
item.dc:creator: Chong-Sun Chu

item.title: The Four-Loop Ladder Integral Family for the QED Electron Self-Energy
item.description: arXiv:2611.32854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the complete set of master integrals of the four-loop ladder integral family contributing to the electron self-energy in Quantum Electrodynamics. We obtain the results through canonical differential equations and write them as iterated integrals over integration kernels related to different parametrizations of the sunrise elliptic curve and a Calabi-Yau threefold. The rich structure of geometries and couplings between them requires the introduction of a large number of extra transcendental functions to reach $\epsilon$-factorization. We discuss explicitly how to find a canonical basis for a selection of particularly interesting sectors. Additionally, we compute local series expansions and numerical boundary constants at $p^2=\infty$ and $p^2=m^2$ up to weight seven, and for the polylogarithmic constants we find analytical representations by numerical matching. The on-shell boundary values of this single family already span all non-polylogarithmic constants entering the planar contribution to the four-loop result for the anomalous magnetic moment $(g-2)$ of the electron. We obtain precise numerical results across all values of $p^2$ using numerical transport.
item.dc:creator: Felix Forner, Andreas von Manteuffel, Christoph Nega, Lorenzo Tancredi

item.title: Fisher information in the flux landscape
item.description: arXiv:2611.32901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We quantify the fine-tuning of the flux superpotential in Type IIB Calabi-Yau orientifold compactifications using the Fisher Information Metric. Treating the background fluxes as model parameters and the magnitude of the superpotential as the physical observable, we show that the Fisher matrix admits a unique non-zero eigenvalue that bounds the superpotential from above and factorises into axio-dilaton, complex structure components and a bounded factor depending on both moduli and the phase of the superpotential. In the canonical duality frame and over the full flux lattice, this eigenvalue grows linearly with the inverse string coupling and cubically with the complex structure saxions. Specialising to a two modulus orientifold of the degree 18 hypersurface in $\mathbb{P}^4(1,1,1,6,9)$ at large complex structure, we combine the flux integrality with the D3-brane tadpole condition to show that several flux components, including the one driving this growth, are forced to vanish across deep moduli space patches, truncating the twelve-dimensional flux lattice to an eight-dimensional sublattice. The Fisher eigenvalue restricted to these admissible flux directions either approaches a constant or grows at most linearly, much more slowly than over the full lattice.
item.dc:creator: Martin Carrascal, Radu Tatar

item.title: Holographic ensembles and giant gravitons at the Leigh--Strassler fixed point
item.description: arXiv:2611.33072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite-rank observables in holographic quantum field theories provide stringent tests of string and M-theory, but remain challenging to compute when supersymmetry is non-maximal. In this paper, we study the finite rank partition function of the $\mathcal N=1$ Leigh-Strassler CFT, which admits an interacting Fermi-gas description. We compute the partition function explicitly in two ensembles: the canonical ensemble at fixed rank $N$, and the grand canonical ensemble, where $N$ is summed over while its conjugate chemical potential $\mu$ is held fixed. In line with recent proposals, we find that the perturbative large-$N$ and large-$\mu$ expansions in both ensembles are reproduced by the on-shell action and one-loop determinant over Kaluza--Klein modes of type IIB supergravity, with appropriate ensemble-dependent boundary terms. Furthermore, the one-loop partition function of a D3-brane giant graviton precisely matches the leading nonperturbative correction to the boundary partition functions.
item.dc:creator: Jesse van Muiden, De-liang Zhong

item.title: Anomalies and the Berry Phase: From $\pi^0\to\gamma\gamma$ to the geometry of the fermion vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2611.33121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We review the chiral anomaly from a historical perspective, from the $\pi^0\to\gamma\gamma$ puzzle and the work of Adler, Bell and Jackiw, to the Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) term. We then describe how the WZW term was motivated from quantum chromodynamics in 1983-85. Integrating out the non-Abelian gauge fields, that have a gapped spectrum, gives a Nambu-Jona-Lasinio type theory of quarks, and integrating out the quarks, which are gapped by chiral symmetry breaking, gives the WZW model. The fermion determinant splits into a regulator-dependent modulus, which gives the dynamics of mesons, and a universal phase, which is fixed by the anomaly and is the WZW term. Restricted to the collective coordinates of the baryon soliton, the WZW term imposes a U(1) constraint that makes the baryon wave functions monopole harmonics and fixes their spin, statistics and flavour multiplets. We then explain that this phase is a Berry phase: the Schwinger terms of current algebra are the curvature of a U(1) connection on the space of chiral field configurations, and the WZW term is its holonomy, which we call a Berry-Wilson loop. In 1+1 dimensions we write the connection explicitly in terms of Euler angles, exhibiting a Dirac monopole whose quantised charge is the level of the current algebra.
item.dc:creator: Spenta R. Wadia

item.title: Scalar perturbations in extremal Reissner-Nordstr\"om geometry: new methods at work
item.description: arXiv:2611.33123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study scalar radiation emitted by a particle moving along a circular orbit around a four-dimensional extremal Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole. In particular, we calculate the energy fluxes carried by scalar waves to infinity and across the event horizon, as well as the scalar self-force acting on the particle, and express all these quantities as post-Newtonian expansions. Our results for the energy fluxes are in agreement with previous numerical findings in the literature. To solve the radial wave equation, we employ and test two distinct analytic approaches: the first is the so-called \textit{kink method}, a novel alternative stemming from quantum integrability and the second is the Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi method. The perfect agreement of the results highlights the potential of the kink method as a complementary tool for studying wave propagation in black-hole spacetimes.
item.dc:creator: Giorgio Di Russo, Davide Fioravanti, Francesco Olivi, Marco Rossi

item.title: The double copy and perturbative teleparallel gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.33146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we analyze the double copy between gluon and graviton amplitudes within the context of teleparallel gravity. We first set up an effective Lagrangian based on minimal assumptions which reproduces the on-shell amplitudes stemming from the double-copy procedure. By straightforwardly computing the three- and four-point amplitude, this double-copy Lagrangian can be constrained up to a few real parameters when expanding to quartic order. For a specific choice of parameters, we find an exact equivalence with perturbative teleparallel gravity. This suggests that the teleparallel formulation might be well suited to make the double copy more transparent from a Lagrangian viewpoint.
item.dc:creator: Georg Stettinger

item.title: A mathematical perspective on nonplanar on-shell forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.10041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-shell forms are differential forms on the Grassmannian which arise in particle physics. They are defined using bipartite graphs with $n$ distinguished ``boundary'' vertices. Mathematical investigation of on-shell forms has largely focused on the case where the graph is planar, in which case one can utilize combinatorial tools pioneered by Postnikov in the study of the totally nonnegative Grassmannian. In this article, we investigate on-shell forms for arbitrary graphs. We first discuss how to extend various tools from the planar case to arbitrary graphs. We then prove a determinantal formula for a class of on-shell forms which first appeared in physics literature. We explain the relation between this class of forms and the hypertree divisors of $M_{0,n}$, introduced by Castravet--Tevelev.
item.dc:creator: Artyom Lisitsyn, Elizabeth Pratt, Melissa Sherman-Bennett, Jaroslav Trnka

item.title: In-in formalism & $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-product: no contribution from total time derivatives
item.description: arXiv:2611.31272v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the in-in formalism, total time derivatives are sometimes argued to contribute nontrivially to inflationary correlators at the evaluation point, i.e., at the end of inflation. In this paper, we disprove this claim based on the path integral. After formulating the canonical quantization and the regulated path integral of systems with total time derivatives, we derive the $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-ordering, the correct operator ordering on the closed time path. In the $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-ordering, the evaluation point, or the turning point of the in-in contour, is merely an intermediate point and is never an endpoint of the generalized path integral contour. As a result, any apparent boundary contributions at the turning point of the forward and backward branches completely cancel out. We demonstrate this cancellation by re-analyzing examples in the literature, with an emphasis on contact terms associated with the $\mathcal{T}_{C}^{\star}$-ordering overlooked previously.
item.dc:creator: Yohei Ema, Muzi Hong, Ryusuke Jinno, Kyohei Mukaida

item.title: Superdaisy Resummation in Theories with Broken Gauge Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2611.31359v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the partial dressing resummation scheme for the finite-temperature effective potential to the gauge and ghost sectors of spontaneously broken gauge theories and apply the resulting framework to the Standard Model. Going beyond the usual high-temperature treatment, we retain the full mass dependence of the thermal self-energies and determine the scalar, gauge-boson and ghost masses self-consistently from a coupled system of gap equations. The solutions show that corrections beyond the leading $\mathcal{O}(T^2)$ approximation are particularly relevant for the gauge-boson thermal masses, while they induce a comparatively small shift in the scalar spectrum for the benchmark studied. The self-consistent gauge-boson dressing in the longitudinal sector reduces the barrier in the finite-temperature Higgs effective potential. Implementing the resummation in the transverse sector removes the barrier and would seem to exclude a first-order phase transition in accordance with lattice results. While such resummation is not quantitatively reliable, due to the transverse excitations becoming strongly coupled, the results showcase the crucial role played by transverse modes in determining the nature of the electroweak phase transition.
item.dc:creator: Martin M\"unzenberg, Carlos Tamarit

item.title: Locality from Nonlocality: Symmetry Relocalization and Gauging of Lattice Dirac Fermions
item.description: arXiv:2611.31366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatially nonlocal symmetries need not imply nonlocal gauge dynamics. Nonlocal canonical transformations make certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions onsite while retaining sufficient Hamiltonian locality for gauging. Symmetry relocalization yields exact or emergent gauge locality in 1D, 2D, and 3D, subject to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies. In 1D, a Hamiltonian-preserving transformation exchanges onsite vector and nonlocal spectral axial charges of a half-filled chain, enabling local gauging of each and exposing their mixed anomaly. Bosonization identifies momentum-winding T-duality, with a parity-projected operator flowing to a noninvertible topological defect. A nonperturbative norm-resolvent bound proves emergent dynamical gauge locality at finite chemical potential, while a doubled Chern-insulator parent reveals the duality's bulk origin and superconducting extensions reveal hidden compact symmetries. In 2D, the square $\pi$-flux Majorana model shares the Kitaev honeycomb model's single Dirac fermion and odd Pfaffian parity but supports sharp and exponentially local compact charges, the latter with nontrivial Chern topology. Relocalization retains Schwartz locality for asymptotically local gauging, while AIII/AII parents clarify bulk charge origin and parity-anomaly inflow. Two flavors yield compact $U(2)$, a quaternionic invariant, and asymptotically local non-Abelian gauging. In 3D, an exact mixed vector-axial flux response is derived, while a distinct model supports an exponentially local vector $U(1)$ charge with strong quaternionic topology. A nonlocal map makes the charge and Kramers symmetry onsite while preserving exponential Hamiltonian locality. For a compact $SU(2)$ Weyl doublet, a no-go theorem forbids translation-preserving Gaussian onsite relocalization retaining Weyl content and Hamiltonian locality.
item.dc:creator: Lei Su

item.title: Quantum black hole evaporation from thin shell collapse: a complete effective picture
item.description: arXiv:2611.31399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum gravity is expected to play a central role in resolving classical singularities and providing a complete, predictive spacetime picture. In this paper, we develop an effective model inspired by loop quantum gravity that aims to fulfill this expectation, providing a unified description of thin shell collapse, black hole formation, evaporation, and remnant dynamics. The framework exhibits general validity, holding across different effective equations of motion, matter sources, and evaporation laws. Specifically, we incorporate backreaction within a quasi-static approximation, modeling the radiation as null dust and matching the ingoing and outgoing fluxes across an evaporation surface using the Darmois-Israel junction conditions. For an evaporation law governed by the Stefan-Boltzmann law, we find that the final stage of evaporation yields an extremal black hole extending into a new asymptotic region, featuring both event and Cauchy horizons. Conversely, under the Schwinger approach, no event or Cauchy horizons form, instead, a temporary dynamical trapped region emerges, and the resulting spacetime remains globally hyperbolic. Under this variant, our model predicts a horizonless null remnant escaping to future null infinity.
item.dc:creator: Micha{\l} Bobula, Francesco Fazzini

item.title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
item.description: arXiv:2611.31749v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations. We demonstrate how parton functions can be directly obtained in Minkowski space using the Hamiltonian framework. We compute fermion and antifermion PDFs, LCDAs, and decay constants of the vector meson in the Schwinger model for several fermion masses. States in Hilbert space are efficiently represented by tensor networks, with an expressivity that is systematically controlled by a bond dimension. The light-front Wilson line is implemented as a stepwise evolution on the lattice that alternates spatial shifts of an external charge with Trotterized time-evolution steps acting on a matrix product state. All systematic uncertainties are quantified by varying and extrapolating in the lattice spacing, volume, bond dimension, gauge-field truncation, and Trotter step width. The slow growth of the entanglement entropy makes moderate bond dimensions sufficient, which supports the feasibility of using tensor networks for computing light-front matrix elements in more general settings. We confirm that the computed distributions fulfill the expected normalizations, momentum sum rules, and symmetry properties.
item.dc:creator: Mari Carmen Ba\~nuls, Krzysztof Cichy, C. -J. David Lin, Manuel Schneider

item.title: A colored look at anyons and parastatistics
item.description: arXiv:2611.31841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Color Lie (super)algebras were introduced in 1978 by Rittenberg and Wyler as generalizations of ordinary Lie (super)algebras. These color structures, graded by abelian groups, are defined by brackets which satisfy generalized Jacobi identities. Only recently the relevance of color Lie (super)algebras to physical applications has been pointed out and proved. The color framework not only describes, but also provides physical signatures for two broad types of parastatistics (particles beyond ordinary bosons/fermions): i) paraparticles which are exchanged via the permutation group and can exist in any space dimension D and ii) anyons (exchanged via the braid group), which exist up to D=2 space dimensions. This paper presents an update of the recent advancements which motivate a brand new "colored look" at questions involving parastatistics and braid statistics.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Toppan

item.title: Field-Dependent Kinetics, Exact Kinks, and a Moduli-Space Route from Self-Dual Yang-Mills Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.31971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study scalar-field models in 1+1 dimensions with field-dependent kinetic coefficients, motivated by self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) theory as a generator of integrable equations. We derive the Euler-Lagrange equation, traveling-wave reduction, and first integral, and solve the inverse problem: given a kinetic structure and a prescribed tanh kink, which potential makes it exact? A quadratic spatial deformation with a canonical temporal sector yields a sextic potential. We obtain: (i) a closed-form kink energy with a Bogomolny-type formulation, independent of the odd parameter, which nonetheless shapes the energy density asymmetrically; (ii) vacuum curvature relations tying the spectrum to the kinetic function at the vacua; (iii) two propositions on speed families, plus a lemma showing single-speed data probe only one combination of the kinetic functions; (iv) a unified admissibility analysis in which positivity of the spatial kinetic function controls hyperbolicity, the potential bound along the kink, and the vacuum masses; (v) a self-adjoint fluctuation operator with a closed-form potential whose asymptotes are the vacuum masses, an exact translation zero mode, and numerical spectra with no negative mode on the admissible region, evidence for spectral stability. Exact SDYM reductions yield integrable equations, whereas the deformed model is generically non-integrable and cannot be an exact reduction. The correct bridge is the moduli-space route: SDYM reduces to the Bogomolny equations, whose BPS monopole and dyon dynamics produce field-dependent kinetic terms; any smooth one-dimensional moduli metric expands, to second order, to the quadratic model studied here, and the Taub-NUT metric of well-separated dyons gives an explicit realization. Full identification of the sextic potential within a specific gauge-theory moduli dynamics remains open and is formulated as a research program.
item.dc:creator: Ji Wang

item.title: Horizon dynamical entropies and phase space topology
item.description: arXiv:2611.32444v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study phase space topologies induced by infinite-dimensional norms as a means to solve the problem of 'integrability' of Hamiltonian generators corresponding to diffeomorphisms of a null hypersurface, with the specific goal in mind to compare different prescriptions for the dynamical entropy of black holes, which replaces the area in non-stationary regimes. We first show that for a scalar field, there exists a family of norms that would provide integrability for different polarizations. We then show that a single member of this family applies to the gravitational field, and it is given by the Sobolev norm already considered in the literature. The obstruction to the other candidates lies in the semi-positivity of the metric.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Bruno, Simone Speziale

item.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
item.description: arXiv:2611.32485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to the conformal bootstrap.
item.dc:creator: Gefei Cai, Shengzhi Jin, Xin Sun, Baojun Wu

item.title: Teichm\"uller spaces with conical singularities and Virasoro coadjoint orbits
item.description: arXiv:2611.32644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Teichm\"uller spaces of hyperbolic \(0\)-metrics on a disk with ideal boundary and a marked point carrying a conical singularity with angle $\theta = 2\pi \beta$. For all $\beta>0$, we show that $\rm{Teich}^{\beta}(\overline{\mathbb D})\cong S^1\backslash \rm{Diff}(S^1)$, and we construct natural closed 2-forms $\omega_\beta$ induced by the Atiyah-Bott construction. For non-integer $\beta$, the form $\omega_\beta$ is symplectic, and one can identify $\rm{Teich}^{\beta}(\overline{\mathbb D})$ with the corresponding elliptic Virasoro coadjoint orbit. For positive integers $\beta=n$, $\omega_\beta$ is presymplectic, and it descends to the Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau symplectic form on the exceptional Virasoro orbit $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)\backslash\rm{Diff}(S^1)$. Infinitesimal isometries of a hyperbolic \(0\)-metric on a disk with a conical singularity with angle $\theta=2\pi n$ are given by the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb R)$ which integrates to the group $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)$ on the boundary of the disk but not in the interior for $n>1$. It is remarkable that the presymplectic structure of the corresponding Teichm\"uller spaces recovers this group and descends to the corresponding Virasoro coadjoint orbit.
item.dc:creator: Anton Alekseev, Rea Dalipi, Samson Shatashvili

item.title: A Systematic Construction of High-Corank Kac--Moody Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.32666v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We form a hexagonal prism from two six-cycles and iterate a doubling construction with a fixed positive integer edge multiplicity, producing a family of indefinite Kac--Moody algebras. The prism's spectrum determines the exact corank of every algebra in the family. Along each nonvanishing parity class, the corank grows exponentially, while its ratio to the matrix size tends to zero. For the twelve-node algebra we identify the two central directions, describe the first two graded levels, and characterize the integral central charges of its unitary highest-weight modules.
item.dc:creator: Beaudoin Simon, Bonnefoy Quentin, Marrani Alessio, Rausch de Traubenberg Michel, Saulquin Victor

item.title: Krylov dynamics of deformed oscillator chains: localization, ballistic spreading, and indeterminacy
item.description: arXiv:2611.32694v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Krylov and spread complexity map quantum dynamics onto a quantum walk on a half-line whose hopping amplitudes are the Lanczos coefficients, so that Krylov dynamics is the theory of orthogonal polynomials and Jacobi operators. We use this correspondence to study Krylov chains generated by the two-parameter $(p,q)$-deformed oscillator, which interpolates between the Heisenberg--Weyl chain, the $q$-oscillator chain of double-scaled SYK, and chains with exponentially growing Lanczos coefficients. For the deformed displacement chain the spread complexity is the mean excitation number, its rate is the deformed momentum quadrature, and its acceleration is $\ddot C_K=2\omega^2\langle[a,a^\dagger]\rangle$, so the deformed commutator acts as a force along the Krylov chain and the mean deformation controls early-time growth. The deformation parameters separate four regimes. For $\max(p,q)<1$ the complexity stays bounded, a localization produced by the algebra alone. For $p=1$, $q<1$ it grows ballistically, with an exact asymptotic velocity given by a theta-type series. At $p=q=1$ it grows as $t^2$. For $\max(p,q)>1$ the Jacobi operator is not essentially self-adjoint, the moment problem is indeterminate, and the Lanczos coefficients no longer determine the dynamics. Even and odd truncations converge to two different evolutions, the two reflection-symmetric N-extremal solutions of the moment problem, the odd one carrying a zero-energy atom of closed-form weight; the self-adjoint extensions yield a family of complexity curves that coincide at early times and separate once the Krylov wavefront reaches infinity. Krylov complexity in this regime is thus defined only once a boundary condition at infinite Krylov index is specified. The orthogonal-polynomial procedure and its checks on exactly solvable chains are given in the appendices.
item.dc:creator: Tunde Joseph Osunmusanmi

item.title: Perturbative unitarity bounds from qubit entanglement in scalar scattering and QED
item.description: arXiv:2611.32842v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the framework of $2\to 2$ relativistic scattering described by the perturbative $S$-matrix, we perform a comprehensive analysis of the properties of quantum channels obtained by tracing out the momentum from the scattered state. We work in two distinct scenarios with qubit degrees of freedom: flavored scalar contact interactions and QED, focusing in particular on initial-state leptons with transverse polarization. We identify the conditions that make the quantum channel unitary, calculate the entanglement of the qubits through the concurrence, and use its maximally allowed value to extract perturbativity upper bounds on the coupling constants. We find that the limits are often more constraining than the corresponding partial-wave expansion bounds, and that they allow us to bypass some of the obstacles associated in the latter with the singular behavior of forward scattering.
item.dc:creator: Shiuli Chatterjee, Kamila Kowalska, Enrico Maria Sessolo

item.title: Strong hyperbolicity of puncture-gauge formulations of gravitational theories with second order equations of motion
